neighbours.label: a function word leading into praise of an outstanding quality or record (wonders| of the world, in| a world record, noted for| his strength)
fire: As a child she was hailed as one of the great piano prodigies of the century.
The sprinter crossed the line in a new world record that still stands today.
The general was famous for his courage, cunning and iron discipline.
Scouts rate him as the best young goalkeeper in the whole league.
The cheetah, the fastest of all land animals, can reach 110 km per hour.
Critics praised the chef for her extraordinary talent with simple ingredients.
The cathedral was considered one of the marvels of the medieval world.
Her serve is what truly sets her apart from every other player on tour.
quiet: As a child she took piano lessons twice a week at the local school.
The sprinter crossed the line in fourth place and walked back to the tunnel.
The general was born in a small village near the northern border.
Scouts watched him play in goal for the reserve team last Sunday.
The cheetah, a member of the cat family, lives mostly on open plains.
Critics noted that the chef had moved her restaurant to a new street.
The cathedral was built over two centuries in the medieval town.
Her serve is something she practises for an hour before every match.

notes: Card: peaks on ' of', ' as', ' a', ' his', ' at', ' almost' right before a superlative or praise (musical wonders of the world, fastest land animals such as, a world record, noted for his strength, Russian 'выдающееся'). The - pole is the much stronger 'before tall' height detector.
